entities.summary: Kėdainiai is a city in Lithuania. It is located on the banks of the Nevėžis river 45 km (28 mi) north of Kaunas, Lithuania's second largest city. One of the oldest settlements in the country, Kėdainiai was first mentioned in the 1372 Livonian Chronicle of Hermann de Wartberge, and became a city in 1590. Its population as of 2022 was 23,051. The Kėdainiai Old Town dates to the 17th century and many of its historical buildings were preserved. Kėdainiai is a city in Northern Europe, established around 1590. Holds notable historical significance, documented across 65 language editions of Wikipedia. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Kėdainiai's historical significance lies in its well-preserved Old Town and its establishment as a city in 1590, making it a notable regional center in Northern Europe. Its population of 23,051 as of 2022 underscores its continued relevance.
